messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Logarithmic y-axis scale with barchart
parts:
Hi:

Question: Since bar charts are anchored at zero (on a frequency scale)
by definition, what is log(0)? Consequently, why would you want to
supply a logarithmic scale to a bar chart? Perhaps a frequency polygon
would be more appropriate if you want to express frequency on a
logarithmic scale (assuming, of course, that all of the class
frequencies are >= 1); see geom_freqpoly().

To

HTH,
Dennis

> barchart. This is done in ggplot2 0.9.1
>
> DF2 <- data.frame(label=c("a","b"),hits=c(20865,127135230))
> p <- ggplot() + geom_bar(data=DF2,aes(x=label,y=hits)) +scale_y_log10()
>
>
> Does anyone have a suggestion as to how I can fix this, so I have a proper

>
> Best,

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Logarithmic y-axis scale with barchart
parts:
My response was to the suggestion of using log(freq + 1/6) to scale
frequencies. Since bar charts are anchored at y = 0, it is considered
a Bad Idea to use a logarithmic scale to represent frequencies. The
issue has been debated on this list several times and I don't intend
to rehash it. IMO, using log(x + 1/6) or whatever is a cosmetic fix to
the problem, but if anyone wants to implement such a scale, they're
welcome to do so. The tools are in the scales package.

I suggested geom_freqpoly() because it doesn't require a geometric
object that is anchored at zero, but it has the same scaling problems
if a category has zero frequency. OTOH, if you have large frequencies
in every category, the vertical axis won't have to contain zero
frequency, unlike a bar chart.

> DF <- data.frame(label=c("a","b"),num=c(1,10))
> p <- ggplot() + geom_bar(data=DF,aes(x=label,y=num)) + scale_y_log10()

This is clever, but you had to manipulate the concept of the bar chart
to achieve your end.

Let's go back to your original example:

ggplot() + geom_bar(data=DF2,aes(x=label,y=hits)) +scale_y_log10()

What's the value at the anchor on the log_10 scale?

messages.subject: Re: Logarithmic y-axis scale with barchart
parts:
Hello,

geom_freqpoly does not work for what I want to show. My data is
structured as follows:
for a given serverA I have X1 submissions
For a given serverB I have X2 submissions
.... And so on.

What I need to produce is a chart that compares the number of
distributions pr. server, and I thought a barchart would be ideal for
this. The two numbers I posted, 20865 and 127135230, are the two
extremes (minimum and maximum), of my data. I have quite a few servers
which are between the minimum and 30k submissions, and on a barchart
it looks like they have zero submissions, which is actually not true,
it's just that other servers have ~6000 times as many submissions. I
thought I would try to correct for this by changing the scale of the
y-axis to a logarithmic one but alas, that seems to be difficult. I
also tried to change the 'starting label' to 20000 by using ylim, but
that does not seem to work.

I must also have been really tired when I posted that last email, the
last example does not seem to produce what I thought it did back then.
My apologies. Also, I don't really understand what you mean by 'but
you had to manipulate the concept of the bar chart to achieve your

end.'

Any advice on the above problem is highly appreciated.

Best,
David
